summary.headline: Allcargo Terminals Q2 FY27 revenue rose 21.5% YoY to INR252 crore and PAT 85% to INR21 crore, helped by transshipment gains that management expects to taper.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 volumes reached 1,90,100 TEUs (+12.6% YoY) and revenue INR252 crore (+21.5% YoY, +17.4% QoQ). EBITDA excluding other income was INR59 crore (+45.9% YoY), with EBITDA per TEU at INR3,366 (+40.8% YoY). Management attributed part of the margin and realisation gain to transshipment (ITP) volumes linked to Gulf-related disruptions, which it expects to fade over the next few quarters. Management said October 2026 was the highest-volume month in company history, and announced a roughly INR400 crore capex plan with dividend policy under review.

segments.name: Container terminals / CFS (India)
segments.commentary: Utilisation at roughly 90-95% across terminals per management; October 2026 recorded the highest monthly volume in company history, driven by JNPA-linked growth in Chennai and Kolkata.

segments.name: Transshipment (ITP)
segments.commentary: Contributed about INR500 per TEU of margin and about INR400-450 per TEU of EBITDA per TEU in Q2; management expects gains to taper over the next few months as Gulf-related disruption eases.

segments.name: Speedy JNPT facility
segments.commentary: Currently handles close to 8,000 TEUs; renovation is underway with a target of about 18,000 TEUs once upgrade completes.

guidance_outlook: Rate increases taken in Q2 expected to largely persist; transshipment-driven revenue and margin uplift expected to taper down, with the margin benefit lasting roughly one more quarter.
Other operating efficiency and yield gains are expected to sustain margins apart from the transshipment effect, per management.
Farukhnagar ICD: PFT construction to finish by end of FY27 with limited operations starting early FY28; ICD construction to complete by end Q3 FY28 and full operations in Q4 FY28.
Chennai 120,000 TEU facility: land finalisation targeted by end of November 2026, customs clearance application to follow, construction to start in Q1 FY28, about 9 months to build.

Dividend payout to be evaluated over the next 6 months, pending M&A and organic opportunities; about INR400 crore internal capex requirement plus INR200-250 crore debt capacity, with leverage possibly up to 1:1.
capex_capacity: Capex requirement of about INR400 crore covering Farukhnagar ICD, Chennai capacity, JNPT expansion and Speedy renovation.
Chennai facility of about 120,000 TEU capacity planned close to the Kattupalli and Ennore terminals.
Farukhnagar ICD: discussions with multiple prospective customers have started; management reports strong positive responses.
Terminal utilisation at 90-95% across the portfolio, which management cites as the reason for capacity expansion.
Speedy JNPT: about 8,000 TEUs today, targeted at about 18,000 TEUs post-upgrade.
demand_pricing: Revenue per TEU reported at INR14,388 in Q2; excluding ITP, INR13,900, versus around INR12,800 in prior quarters, attributed to ITP mix and a rate increase taken in Q2.
Management said competitive intensity across its CFS locations is broadly unchanged.
Management cited India port cargo growth of 10-12%, with CFS volumes growing at a similar pace.
National trade: H1 FY27 total exports about $476 billion (+13.84% YoY) and imports about $551 billion (+15.68% YoY), as stated by management.
Geopolitical disruption raised freight rates, transit times and localised container imbalances during the quarter.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the revenue per TEU increase came from transshipment mix versus rate increases?
qa_highlights.answer: Reported revenue per TEU INR14,388 (INR13,900 ex-ITP) versus about INR12,800 earlier; ITP adds about INR400-450 to EBITDA per TEU. Rate increases taken this quarter also contributed alongside better cargo mix.

qa_highlights.question: Will revenue per TEU normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Rate impacts are largely expected to persist; transshipment volume and revenue should taper as the Gulf-related situation normalises.

qa_highlights.question: Has competitive intensity changed at the CFS locations?
qa_highlights.answer: No major change; the competitive scenario is more or less the same as before.

qa_highlights.question: Are other and employee expenses run-rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Employee cost is normal and recurring; other expenses include about INR1 crore of one-time consultancy costs that will fall away.

qa_highlights.question: Update on the Chennai 120,000 TEU facility?
qa_highlights.answer: Land finalisation targeted by end-November 2026, customs application to follow, construction in Q1 FY28, about 9 months to build; it sits near Kattupalli and Ennore.

qa_highlights.question: Dividend payout outlook after the capex cycle?
qa_highlights.answer: Management will assess over about 6 months given M&A and organic options; roughly INR400 crore internal capex plus INR200-250 crore debt capacity, with leverage possibly up to 1:1.

risks_watch: Transshipment-driven margin and realisation gains are expected to fade over the next few quarters, which could pull EBITDA per TEU back toward the prior run-rate.
Execution risk on Farukhnagar ICD, Chennai facility and the Speedy JNPT upgrade, with timelines dependent on land, customs and construction milestones.
Global trade disruption (geopolitics, freight rates, container imbalances) could alter volume mix.
Dividend and capital allocation remain undecided pending M&A evaluation; debt could rise to about 1:1 leverage.
Speedy JNPT utilisation is currently low (about 8,000 TEUs) and depends on infrastructure upgrades.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volumes and demand, with October called a record month, but cautious and somewhat non-committal on dividends, M&A and the medium-term trajectory, which management referred to a previously shared five-year plan rather than quantifying.
key_quotes: Our container volumes grew by 12.6% year-on-year.
For this month of October itself, we have achieved highest volumes in the ATL history.
The rate impacts are there to stay for coming quarters largely.

growth.why: No explicit numeric revenue growth guidance; management expects transshipment-driven revenue and margin uplift to taper over the next few quarters, with ~INR400 crore capex and new capacity (Chennai 120k TEU, Farukhnagar ICD, Speedy upgrade) mostly arriving from FY28, while utilisation of 90-95% supports near-term volumes.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA per TEU at INR3,366 (+16.1% QoQ) is flattered by ITP worth about INR400-450 per TEU, which management expects to taper over about one more quarter, while other efficiency and yield gains are said to sustain margins.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: Q4 FY28 (Speedy and Farukhnagar); Chennai build Q1 FY28
rows.why: Utilisation at 90-95% across terminals drives Chennai 120,000 TEU (construction Q1 FY28, about 9 months), Farukhnagar ICD (limited ops early FY28, full Q4 FY28) and Speedy JNPT (8,000 to 18,000 TEU) but these mostly land beyond the 2-4 quarter window.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: October 2026 was the record month and India port cargo growth is 10-12% with CFS volumes growing at a similar pace; H1 FY27 volumes +10% YoY with Q2 +12.6%, though ITP volumes are expected to fade.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.when: already committed; land by end Nov 2026
rows.why: Utilisation at 90-95% has led to about INR400 crore capex plan already announced across Farukhnagar, Chennai, JNPT and Speedy, with Chennai land targeted by end-November 2026.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No numeric guidance raise; management expects transshipment-driven revenue and margin uplift to taper over the next few quarters.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Revenue per TEU of INR14,388 includes ITP; ex-ITP is INR13,900 vs about INR12,800 earlier, and the ITP-driven uplift is expected to fade as Gulf disruption eases, so the margin base could reset lower.

rows.label: Rate increases taken in Q2 persist
rows.why: Revenue per TEU ex-ITP at INR13,900 vs about INR12,800 earlier, and management says Q2 rate increases should largely persist.

rows.label: Dividend policy review and leverage up to 1:1
rows.why: Management will assess dividend over about 6 months with INR200-250 crore debt capacity and INR650 crore deployable in 1-1.5 years, pending M&A options.

rows.label: One-time consultancy costs fall away
rows.why: About INR1 crore of one-time consultancy costs in other expenses will not recur, a small support to EBITDA.

tone.note: Management was confident on record October volumes, 90-95% utilisation and rate persistence, but cautious on dividends, M&A and the medium-term trajectory; analysts probed how much of the revenue per TEU gain was ITP mix versus rate increases.
